datasets.title: Satellite detected waters in Quezon Province, Bicol Region (Region V) of Philippines as of 12 November 2020
datasets.description: UNOSAT code: TC20201111PHL This map illustrates satellite-detected surface waters in Calauag and Lopez municipalities of Quezon province of Philippines as observed from a Sentinel-1 image acquired on 12 November 2020 at 05:38 local time. Within the analyzed area of about 260 km2, a total of about 20 km2 of lands appear to be flooded. Based on Worldpop population data and the detected surface waters, about 8,300 people are potentially exposed or living close to flooded areas. This is a preliminary analysis and has not yet been validated in the field. Please send ground feedback to UNITAR-UNOSAT. Important Note: Flood analysis from radar images may underestimate the presence of standing waters in built-up areas and densely vegetated areas due to backscattering properties of the radar signal.. [Source: This metadata record was automatically extracted from the Humanitarian Data Exchange (HDX); Original dataset: https://data.humdata.org/dataset/waters-in-quezon-province-bicol-region-region-v-of-philippines-as-of-12-november-2020]
datasets.details: This is a preliminary assessment and has not yet been validated in the field. It is important to consider the characteristics of the source imagery used in the analyses when interpreting results. For damage assessments it should be noted that only significant damage to the structural integrity of the buildings analyzed can be seen in imagery, while minor damage such as cracks or holes may not be visible at all. For flood extractions using radar data it is important to note that urban areas and highly vegetated areas may mask the flood signature and result in underestimation of flood waters. Users with specific questions or concerns should contact unosat@unitar.org to seek clarification.

lineage.description: Sentinel-1 SAR imagery acquired on 12 November 2020 was analyzed by UNOSAT through visual interpretation and change detection to identify satellite-detected surface waters in Quezon Province. Detected flood extent (~20 km²) was intersected with WorldPop population data to estimate approximately 8,300 people potentially exposed to flooded areas. This is a preliminary post-event damage assessment product.
